sections.title: Grantsmanship for Career Development Awards
sections.description: Open to nondegree: No Prerequisite: Students are required to be writing a career development award during the term in which they enroll in the course. If you are interested in taking the course,  please contact Dr. Rachel Locke to confirm you meet the requirements before requesting permission to register. Objectives: (1) Write a first draft of the Candidate Section of the K award (and more if your Specific Aims are clear and don’t change considerably during the course). (2) Understand and apply grant writing best practices to basic science and translational research grants beyond NIH. (3) Develop professional networks with other students.   Topics covered: (1) How to Apply to NIH: NIH lingo; Reading NOFOs; Finding all the instructions; Grant review and scoring; Biosketch.  (2) Writing Career Development Awards (K): The concept behind these awards; How to write the 3 parts of the Candidate Section; Identifying your career niche, career goals, and the skills you need to succeed in your niche; Writing the training plan: activities will you do to gain the skills you need, who will help you get those skills (identifying mentors and advisory committee members); Letters of Reference.  (3) The Research Project: Grants solve problems that people in your field care about; What is your grant story?; Creating a graphical representation of your Specific Aims; Developing clarity about data output, interpretation, value, potential and where on the application you use each concept; Linking your preliminary data to the Specific Aims; Writing hypotheses: Presenting preliminary data and figures in grants; Grant planning using the statement of work; Your grant story’s happy ending: framing your application. (4) How to write the Specific Aims Page: structure. (5) How to write the Approach Section: structure. (6) How to write the Significance section: structure. What is the Innovation section about, anyway? (7) How to save hours of your precious life by using the Styles in MS Word. Approach: To achieve the course objectives, we will use: didactic presentations by the course director, outside experts, and students; group/partner discussions; in-class exercises and worksheets; weekly homework assignments.

sections.title: Grantsmanship
sections.description: Prerequisite: Students are required to be writing a career development award during the term in which they enroll in the course. If you are interested in taking the course, but unsure if you meet the requirements, contact Dr. Rachel Locke. Students will learn to write a mentored career development award (i.e. NIH K23, K08, Foundation CDA). More specifically, students will: Understand how grant proposals are reviewed by NIH and which NIH resources are available to investigators Learn how to find and follow the multiple sets of instructions that apply to many NIH proposals Develop a method to assemble, write and track the parts of an application Write an organized and concise Specific Aims page Develop a research proposal that specifically addresses review criteria Gain an improved understanding of how to present your statistical analysis Review classmates’ proposals and receive coaching on how to improve their own proposal Understand how to develop a budget and how budgets are handled in the University system
